verdict: Both pages are fetched about equally often. Xflow's is quoted once per fetch, Skydo's once in six. The gap is in how the content is shaped, not in reach.

metrics.note: Xflow is longer but split into far smaller units.
Xflow writes one claim per paragraph. Skydo writes prose blocks.
Each Xflow bullet is a standalone, quotable claim under a brand heading.
Xflow gives every alternative its own H3 and five H4 sub-blocks. Skydo's alternative cards carry no headings at all in the crawled text.

diagnosis: Answer in the first sentence. Xflow's opening line is the ranked list. ChatGPT's answer to 'wise alternatives' is a ranked list, so the page already looks like the answer. Skydo's first 130 words describe Wise and show a calculator.

Name the competitors. A 'Wise alternatives' page that names one fintech cannot feed a seven-item answer. Xflow names Skydo with correct pricing and still ranks first; naming rivals cost it nothing and earned it citations on Skydo's own facts.

One heading per brand, one bullet per claim. Xflow's 105 brand bullets are each a quotable sentence under an H3 that carries the brand name. Skydo's cards have no heading, and the brand name is fused to the descriptor in the crawled text, so a claim cannot be attributed to a brand without reading the whole card.
Tables need text headers. Skydo's feature table is the strongest fact block on the page and ChatGPT cannot read it, because the column headers are logos.
Date the numbers and label the estimates. 'about ₹93,200, as of July 2026' is copied into answers with the hedge intact. Undated numbers are treated as claims.
Show your method. 'How we chose' and 'How we verified' are two short sections that make a vendor page read like a review.
Author, verifier, dates, BlogPosting schema. Skydo's page has none of them.
Fewer CTAs, no carousel. Eleven 'Try Skydo Today' lines and a duplicated card are noise between the facts.
spec: Rewrite the H1 to include the query verbatim: 'Best Wise alternatives for receiving international payments in India (2026)'.
First sentence: the ranked list of named platforms. Suggested: Skydo, Xflow, Payoneer, Airwallex, Infinity, BriskPe, Winvesta. Keep Skydo first, give the others accurate numbers.

Replace the method carousel with seven static brand sections, each an H3 with the brand name and H4 blocks: Best for (one sentence), Key features (5 bullets), Pros (4), Cons (4), Verdict (one line). Skydo's block should include the honest con about small invoices.
Keep the feature table but put text in the header cells, and add a net-₹ table at $1,000 / $5,000 / $10,000 dated 'as of <month> 2026'.
Add 'How we chose' (4 criteria) and 'How we verified' (sources, dates) sections.
Add author, verifier, published and updated dates, and BlogPosting plus Person schema.
Cut CTAs to four: after the shortlist, after the table, after the Skydo block, at the end.
Move the methods (SWIFT, PayPal, Stripe, Dodo, remittance) into one 'Other ways to receive payments' section below the seven brands, or link to the landing page that already covers them.
Success check after 30 days: citations per retrieval on this URL above 0.5 (today 0.16), and ChatGPT lifting at least one non-Skydo claim from the page.

playbook.use_when: The query is '<brand> alternatives', '<brand> competitors' or 'best alternatives to <brand> in India'. ChatGPT's answer is a ranked list of named platforms with a one-line role each and a use-case table. Five teardowns sit in this bucket: Wise, PayPal, Payoneer, Stripe and Xflow alternatives.
blueprint: Title and H1 contain the query verbatim: 'Best <Brand> alternatives for receiving international payments in India (2026)'.
Byline: author, verifier, published and updated dates. BlogPosting and Person schema.
First sentence is the ranked list of named platforms. Seven names. Skydo first, competitors named honestly, including Xflow, Infinity, BriskPe, Airwallex, Winvesta where they fit.
Two-sentence 'why people leave <Brand>' with the specific triggers (percentage fee grows, entity restriction, FIRA not automatic).
Shortlist block: 7 bullets, brand in bold, one line each.
Comparison table with text column headers: Platform / Fee model / Best for / About on a $1,000 invoice, dated 'as of <month> 2026'. Second table: net INR at $2,000 / $5,000 / $10,000.
'How we chose' with 4 criteria, and a compliance-fit block: PA-CB status and FIRA handling per brand with dates.

One H3 per brand, numbered. Under each: H4 Best for (one sentence), H4 Key features (5-6 bullets), H4 Pros (4), H4 Cons (4), H4 Verdict (one line). Give competitors accurate numbers and give Skydo an honest con.
'How to choose' with 4 bullets keyed to entity type, invoice size, compliance, and how you get paid.

Open with the query's decisive split in the first two paragraphs (Payoneer: marketplace payouts vs direct invoices; Stripe: gateway vs merchant of record vs invoice collection). Skydo's Payoneer page wins its query because it does this.

Name every brand ChatGPT's answer names for that query, including the ones that are not receiving accounts (Razorpay, Cashfree, PayU for PayPal and Stripe; PingPong, Airwallex, Infinity for Payoneer; Airwallex, Infinity, Veem for Xflow). A missing brand is a row sourced from a competitor.
Give Skydo an honest con on its own page. In every bucket, the page ChatGPT cites for Skydo's description is the competitor page that states Skydo's cons.
'How we verified this' with sources and dates. FAQ of 6-7 questions with factual two-sentence answers.
Label estimates 'about' and your own numbers 'exact'. 3,000-3,500 words is fine when it is 100+ bullets and short paragraphs.
Four CTAs at most. Static HTML: no carousel, no logo-only table headers, no calculator in the crawled text.
